text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The National Assembly has announced that nationwide elections for the legislature's next five-year term will be held on July 20.
-- Belarussian President Alexander Lukashenko will arrive in Hnaoi on Wednesday for a five-day visit.
-- The Japanese government plans to earmark some $87 million from its aid of $640 million to Vietnam in 1997 for upgrading Hnaoi's infrastructure.
-- Five Chinese fishing boats with 62 fishermen were captured by Vietnamese forces on April 13 while using explosives for fishing of central coastal city of Da Nang.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has urged local authorities to stop migration to the central highland to prevent further environment and forest destruction.
-- Vietnam and China have agreed to quicken the tempo of negotiations on their land borders, sea boundaries in Tonkin Gulf and other maritime issues.
-- Prime Minister Vo Van Kiet has instructed local authorities to organise experimental working teams under army management to build part of the country's new north-south expressway.
-- State budget revenues reached 21.6 percent of the whole year's target by mid-April.
